notes: 1. SM master OTP = 258369; UAT SM mobile = 8888888888. SM portal login is at https://uat-web.xrportal.in/sales-manager (Mobile-OTP only, no password). Successful login lands on Callback Requests (default), NOT Towers. The Tower Heatmap lives at /sales-manager/towers (sidebar label 'Towers', page heading h5 'Tower View').

2. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT record/state (e.g. a unit that can be put on HOLD/BOOKED during an active campaign, an admin-disabled tower, a non-SM mobile, or a valid API bearer token) must be supplied before executing this test. Tower Heatmap is read-only, so this almost always means setup performed from another surface (Admin Portal / Physical Allocation).
3. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS; confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative.

4. Tower Heatmap is a READ/VISUALISATION surface only. SMs cannot change unit status from this screen (SM-BRD §4 rule 9, SM-FS §1.2/§1.6.1). No write controls, no allocate/book/hold/reserve buttons. To allocate, SM uses the Physical Allocation module (/sales-manager/physical-allocation) — see SM-FS 'How to Use' Step 4. No audit-log row is written for viewing (SM-FS §1.7).

5. HEATMAP COLOUR GLOSSARY (source-verified — SM-FS FSD-CORRECTION 2026-05-25, common.service.js): GREEN #00FF00 = AVAILABLE / HOLD / PREBOOKED / RESERVED (all four states share one green bucket); RED #FF0000 = BOOKED / PBT; GREY #808080 = REFUGE / NOT_AVAILABLE (synthetic padding). ORANGE and BLUE colours from the old SM-FS §1.5 legend table DO NOT EXIST in source (max-preferences orange highlight code is commented out; blue 'Reserved' is folded into the green bucket).

6. LIVE CSS CLASS -> STATUS MAP (visual-memory _heatmap-unit-classes.json, Tower 9 - Triumph, 280 cells): available-unit (223, white bg + green outline, clickable -> Unit Details panel), disabled-unit (29, grey, inert), booked-unit (7, red, inert), refuse-area refuge-unit (6, light grey, text 'REFUGE', inert), pbt-unit (2, rendered cyan/turquoise in UAT, inert), not-available-unit (13, grey, inert). Only available-unit cells are interactive. The left-rail tower-item 'X Units Available' badge equals that tower's available-unit cell count.

7. DOC_DRIFT-001 (legend) — SM-FS §1.5 table (White/Green=Available, Orange=Hold, Red=Booked, Blue=Reserved) is STALE and contradicted by the SM-FS FSD-CORRECTION block and source. The corrected 3-colour map (green/red/grey, no orange, no blue) is canonical. BRD/FRD legend table must be rewritten to the corrected map. TC generation uses the OBSERVED/corrected values; legacy orange/blue TCs (SM_HMP_005/007/008) are retained but re-expected to the corrected map and tagged DOC_DRIFT-001.

8. DOC_DRIFT-002 (PBT colour) — Source FSD-CORRECTION places PBT in the RED bucket (#FF0000), but the UAT live capture renders pbt-unit cells in cyan/turquoise. Visual evidence contradicts the source colour map for PBT only. [VERIFY WITH DEV] whether cyan is current source-of-truth or stale CSS. (TC_SMTWR_FUNC_012.)

9. DOC_DRIFT-003 (hover tooltip) — visual-memory INDEX.md states NO separate tooltip element renders on hover (hover is a pure CSS border effect on the cell); legacy TC SM_TH_026 asserts a tooltip/popover with unit number + status appears. INDEX.md (live DOM) is canonical: hover shows no tooltip. SM_TH_026 retained but re-expected to 'no tooltip element' and tagged DOC_DRIFT-003; the unit number is read by clicking an available cell (Unit Details panel), not by hover.

10. DOC_DRIFT-004 (default landing after login) — SM-FRD §6 says /sales-manager redirects to /sales-manager/callback-requests; Towers is reached via the sidebar. Any flow expecting Towers as the post-login landing is wrong. (TC_SMTWR_NEG_028 / TC_SMTWR_FUNC_029.)

11. There is NO discrete filter UI on Tower View (no status dropdown, no BHK selector, no floor filter). Filtering happens only via tower selection in the left rail; floor labels are read-only. heatmap-filter.png is a fallback capture documenting the absence (visual-memory INDEX.md).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Tower View page loads at /sales-manager/towers
tcs.description: Verify that the Tower Heatmap page renders when an SM navigates to the Towers route.
tcs.precond: SM is logged in; at least one tower is configured and active.
tcs.steps:
1. From the sidebar (or bottom navigation) click 'Towers'.
2. Wait for the page to finish loading.
tcs.expected: The URL changes to /sales-manager/towers and the page renders the h5 heading 'Tower View' with no errors.

tcs.scenario: To verify sidebar navigation from Callback Requests to Towers
tcs.description: Verify that clicking the Towers link in the sidebar/bottom-nav from the default Callback Requests page opens the Tower View.
tcs.precond: SM is logged in and on /sales-manager/callback-requests (default landing).
tcs.steps:
1. Click the 'Towers' link/icon in the sidebar or bottom navigation.
2. Confirm the route changes.
tcs.expected: The URL changes to /sales-manager/towers, the Tower View loads with the default tower selected and grid rendered, and the nav indicator highlights 'Towers' as the active tab.

tcs.scenario: To verify the default tower is auto-selected on first load
tcs.description: Verify that on first load a default tower is pre-selected and its grid is rendered without a manual click.
tcs.precond: SM logged in; session in automation-repository/fixtures/.auth/sales-manager.json; at least one active tower configured.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to https://uat-web.xrportal.in/sales-manager/towers.
2. Wait for the left rail 'Select Tower' and the right pane 'Tower View' to render.
3. Observe which tower carries the selected-tower highlight in the left rail.
tcs.expected: Page loads with h5 'Tower View'. The left rail shows 'Select Tower' with description 'Choose a tower to view available units'. A default tower (Tower 8 - Crest in UAT) is pre-selected with a green-background highlight. The right pane title reads 'Tower: Crest' and its unit grid is rendered. No manual click is required to see units.

2. Inspect which tower is selected by default.
3. Verify its grid has loaded.
tcs.expected: The first active tower (or the last-viewed tower from session/local storage if persisted) is selected by default and its grid is loaded. [VERIFY WITH DEV] whether last-viewed persistence is implemented or it is always the first tower.

tcs.scenario: To verify selecting a tower loads its unit grid

tcs.scenario: To verify switching towers updates the grid

tcs.scenario: To verify only one tower is selected at a time across repeated switches
tcs.description: Verify the selected-tower highlight is exclusive and the grid never retains stale content across switches.
tcs.precond: At least 2 towers visible in the left rail.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the initial selected tower (Tower 8 - Crest, default).
2. Click 'Tower 9 - Triumph'.
3. Click 'Tower 8 - Crest' again.
4. Click 'Tower 11 - Prime'.
tcs.expected: Only one tower carries the selected highlight at any moment. After step 2 only Tower 9 is selected; after step 3 only Tower 8; after step 4 only Tower 11. The right-pane title updates each time and the grid contents fully replace the previous tower's grid (no stale cells).

3. Click the cell.
4. Wait for the right-side 'Unit Details' panel to render.
tcs.expected: Hover applies CSS hover styling on the cell border (no separate tooltip element renders — visual hover only, DOC_DRIFT-003). On click, the 'Unit Details' panel mounts adjacent to the grid (NOT a modal — the grid stays visible). The panel header h5 'Unit Details' with a green background bar appears.

tcs.scenario: To verify the Unit Details panel field set
tcs.description: Verify every field shown in the Unit Details panel for an available unit.
tcs.precond: An available unit clicked (e.g. 3501 in Tower 9 - Triumph).
tcs.steps: 1. With the panel open, read all visible fields.
tcs.expected: The panel shows: Unit No (e.g. '3501 - Triumph'), BHK (e.g. '1 BHK Growth Home'), Size (e.g. '323 sq.ft.'), Agreement Value (masked as '₹ xxxxxxxx' in UAT), Stamp Duty (₹ value), GST (₹ value), Registration Charges (₹ value), and an '*All inclusive' info-icon row showing a total. No 'Allocate'/write-action button is present (read-only).

tcs.scenario: To verify the '*All inclusive' info icon on the Unit Details panel
tcs.description: Verify the all-inclusive total row and its info icon.
tcs.precond: Unit Details panel open for an available unit.
tcs.steps:
1. Locate the '*All inclusive' row at the bottom of the panel.
2. Hover/tap the info icon next to it.
tcs.expected: The '*All inclusive' row shows a total amount (sum of agreement value + stamp duty + GST + registration charges; masked in UAT). The info icon is present. [VERIFY WITH DEV] whether the info icon opens a breakdown tooltip — not documented in BRD/FRD.

tcs.scenario: To verify the panel updates when a different available unit is clicked
tcs.description: Verify that clicking a second available unit replaces the panel content with the new unit's details.
tcs.precond: Unit Details panel open for unit 3501.
tcs.steps:
1. With the panel showing 3501, click a different available unit (e.g. 3505).
2. Read the panel fields again.
tcs.expected: The panel updates in place to show the newly clicked unit's details (Unit No changes to e.g. '3505 - Triumph', and Size/BHK/values update accordingly). The panel does not stack or open a second instance; the grid stays visible.

tcs.scenario: To verify hover on an available cell shows no separate tooltip — DOC_DRIFT-003
tcs.description: Verify the documented contradiction that hover shows only a CSS border effect and no tooltip element.
tcs.precond: Tower selected; available unit grid loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Hover over an available unit cell (desktop).
2. Inspect the DOM for any tooltip/popover element.
tcs.expected: DOC_DRIFT-003: hovering an available cell shows only a CSS border/hover effect on the cell — NO separate tooltip or popover element renders (per visual-memory INDEX.md live DOM). Legacy SM_TH_026 asserting a tooltip is corrected here. The unit number/status is read by CLICKING the cell (Unit Details panel), not by hover.

tcs.scenario: To verify hover/tap behaviour on a unit cell — DOC_DRIFT-003
tcs.description: Verify what hovering (desktop) or tapping (mobile) a unit cell shows, against the corrected no-tooltip evidence.
tcs.precond: Tower selected; unit grid loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Hover over a unit cell (desktop) or tap (mobile).
2. Inspect for any tooltip content.
tcs.expected: DOC_DRIFT-003: INDEX.md (live DOM) shows NO tooltip element renders on hover — only a CSS border effect. The original expectation of a tooltip/popover with unit number + status is NOT met by the live UI. On mobile, a tap on an available cell opens the Unit Details panel instead. [VERIFY WITH DEV] whether a tooltip is intended (BRD/FRD silent).

tcs.scenario: To verify the SM cannot modify unit status from the heatmap
tcs.description: Verify there are no edit/book/hold/status-change controls on the heatmap.
tcs.precond: Tower selected; unit grid loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Click an available unit.
2. Right-click or long-press a unit.
3. Inspect for any edit/action controls.
tcs.expected: No edit, book, hold, or status-change controls are present; the view is read-only per SM-BRD §4 rule 9 / SM-FS §1.6.1.

tcs.scenario: To verify the heatmap exposes no allocation action
tcs.description: Verify there is no allocate/book/hold/reserve action anywhere on the panel or grid.
tcs.precond: An available unit clicked; Unit Details panel open.
tcs.steps:
1. Inspect the Unit Details panel for any 'Allocate'/'Book'/'Hold'/'Reserve' buttons.
2. Right-click a unit cell to check for a context menu.
3. Double-click an available unit.
tcs.expected: No write-action controls exist on the panel or grid; no allocation/booking buttons; no actionable context menu. The Tower View is strictly informational. To allocate a unit to a walk-in customer, the SM uses the Physical Allocation module (/sales-manager/physical-allocation), per the explicit Note in SM-FS 'How to Use' Step 4.

tcs.scenario: To verify non-available cells do not open the Unit Details panel
tcs.description: Verify that booked, refuge, disabled, pbt and not-available cells are all inert on click.
tcs.precond: Tower 9 - Triumph selected.
tcs.steps:
1. Click in sequence: a booked-unit cell, a refuge-unit cell, a disabled-unit cell, a pbt-unit cell, a not-available-unit cell.
2. After each click, check whether the Unit Details panel opens or changes.
tcs.expected: None of the five non-available status cells open or update the Unit Details panel — they are inert on click (per INDEX.md interactions). No console errors. Only available-unit cells are interactive.

tcs.scenario: To verify there is no discrete filter control on Tower View
tcs.description: Verify the absence of any status/BHK/floor filter UI.
tcs.precond: Tower View page loaded.
tcs.steps:
1. Inspect the page chrome above and around the grid for any filter control (status dropdown, BHK selector, floor filter).
2. Confirm absence.
tcs.expected: No discrete filter UI is present. Filtering happens only via tower selection in the left rail; floor labels are read-only (not clickable filters). heatmap-filter.png documents the absence. Current scope: no filters (future BRD changes may add them).

tcs.scenario: To verify no audit-log row is written when the SM views the heatmap
tcs.description: Verify that browsing/clicking on the read-only heatmap produces no audit entries.
tcs.precond: SM logged in. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] audit-log read access.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the current latest audit_log row.
2. SM navigates to /sales-manager/towers and clicks several towers + available units.
3. Query audit_logs for any new entries from this SM in that window.
tcs.expected: No new audit_log rows from this SM (read-only screen, no write events), confirming SM-FS §1.7.

tcs.scenario: To verify no audit trail is expected from heatmap navigation
tcs.description: Verify the no-audit-trail business rule across navigation, switches and panel views.
tcs.precond: SM views the heatmap, clicks units, switches towers.
tcs.steps:
1. Browse the heatmap, switch towers, click multiple available units.
2. Check admin-side audit/activity logs for any entries from this SM session.
tcs.expected: Per SM-FS §1.7 'No write actions occur from this screen — no audit trail required.' No audit entries are produced from heatmap navigation, tower switches, or unit-detail panel views.

tcs.scenario: To verify the grid updates in real time during an active campaign
tcs.description: Verify a unit status change pushed from elsewhere reflects on the SM heatmap without refresh.
tcs.precond: An active allocation campaign is running; SM viewing the heatmap. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] active campaign + a unit to change.
tcs.steps:
1. Keep the heatmap open.
2. Have another user/admin place a unit on HOLD.
3. Observe the SM view.
tcs.expected: The unit's cell transitions in the green bucket (HOLD shares green) without a page refresh, via WebSocket, per SM-FS §1.6 rule 3. [Note: HOLD does not turn orange — DOC_DRIFT-001.]

tcs.scenario: To verify a BOOKED change propagates live and decrements the available badge
tcs.description: Verify a unit becoming BOOKED during a campaign flips the cell to red and lowers the left-rail count.
tcs.precond: A PHYSICAL_EVENT / active allocation campaign is running; SM has /sales-manager/towers open. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] active campaign + bookable unit.
tcs.steps:
1. Note the available-unit count for Tower 9 - Triumph.
2. From a separate Admin/SM session, mark a unit in that tower as BOOKED via Physical Allocation.
3. Wait up to ~5s for the WebSocket push.
4. Inspect the original SM session's grid.
tcs.expected: Per SM-FS §1.6 rule 3, the previously-available cell transitions from available-unit to booked-unit (green -> red) without page refresh, and the available-unit count in the left rail decrements by one.

tcs.scenario: To verify the grid reflects last-known DB state when no campaign is active
tcs.description: Verify that outside an active campaign the view shows the last-known DB state and does not live-update.
tcs.precond: No active PHYSICAL_EVENT campaign running.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to /sales-manager/towers.
2. Inspect a tower's grid.
3. Cross-check available/booked counts against a DB snapshot.
tcs.expected: Per SM-FS §1.6 rule 4, the grid loads with the last-known unit statuses; no real-time updates flow.

tcs.scenario: To verify no live updates flow outside an active campaign
tcs.description: Verify the WebSocket is idle/absent when no campaign is active and the view is static.
tcs.precond: No active allocation campaign; SM viewing the heatmap.
tcs.steps:
1. SM opens /sales-manager/towers.
2. Inspect WebSocket connections in DevTools.
3. Wait ~60s and observe the units.
tcs.expected: Unit colours reflect the most recent DB state; no live updates flow; the WebSocket may be inactive or idle — view matches SM-FS §1.6 rule 4. [VERIFY WITH DEV] whether the socket connects but stays idle, or does not connect at all, outside a campaign.

tcs.scenario: To verify the WebSocket reconnects after a transient network drop
tcs.description: Verify that live updates resume after a brief offline period without a page refresh.
tcs.precond: Active campaign; heatmap open with live updates working. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] active campaign.
tcs.steps:
1. In DevTools set the network Offline for 10s.
2. Set the network back Online.
3. Have an admin change a unit status.
4. Observe the SM heatmap.
tcs.expected: After reconnect, the latest unit-status changes propagate to the SM heatmap with no manual refresh and no stale-state lock. [VERIFY WITH DEV] reconnect behaviour not documented in BRD/FRD.

tcs.scenario: To verify switching towers preserves the live-update subscription
tcs.description: Verify live updates keep flowing for the currently-viewed tower after a tower switch.
tcs.precond: Active campaign; multiple active towers. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] active campaign.
tcs.steps:
1. View Tower A; admin changes a unit status in Tower A -> observe the update.
2. Click Tower B in the sidebar.
3. Admin changes a unit status in Tower B -> observe the update.
tcs.expected: Live updates flow for the currently-viewed tower; switching towers does not break the WebSocket subscription; updates for Tower B arrive in real time. [VERIFY WITH DEV] whether the subscription is re-scoped per tower or is project-wide.

tcs.scenario: To verify logout closes the WebSocket subscription
tcs.description: Verify the live-update socket is closed cleanly on logout with no leaked subscription.
tcs.precond: Active campaign; SM viewing the heatmap with live updates connected. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] active campaign.
tcs.steps:
1. Open DevTools -> Network -> WS and verify the WebSocket is open.
2. Click Logout.
3. Observe the WebSocket state.
tcs.expected: The WebSocket connection closes (status 1000/1001) on logout; no leaked subscription remains after the JWT is cleared. [VERIFY WITH DEV] clean-close not documented.

tcs.scenario: To verify a rapid status-change burst reconciles to final DB state on reload
tcs.description: Verify the UI converges to the canonical DB value after a burst of out-of-order WebSocket frames.
tcs.precond: Active campaign; rapid status changes possible on a unit. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] active campaign.
tcs.steps:
1. Have admin rapidly change a unit AVAILABLE -> HOLD -> BOOKED within 2 seconds.
2. Observe the heatmap during the burst.
3. Refresh the page after it settles.
tcs.expected: The final state on refresh matches the DB final state (BOOKED -> red). Intermediate WebSocket frames may arrive out of order, but a reload reconciles to the canonical DB value. [VERIFY WITH DEV] in-burst rendering order not guaranteed by spec.

tcs.scenario: To verify the heatmap endpoint is shared across roles
tcs.description: Verify the towers/units endpoints return 200 for user/admin/sm-admin/sm JWTs (shared, protect-gated).
tcs.precond: A valid JWT for each role. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] tokens for each role + API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call GET /api/v1/towers and GET /api/v1/towers/:towerId/units with each of the user/admin/sm-admin/sm JWTs.
2. Read the status codes.
tcs.expected: All four roles get HTTP 200. The endpoint is protect-gated and shared. Response shape may vary by an ?action= query param. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm per-role payload differences.

tcs.scenario: To verify the ?action= query param scopes the response shape
tcs.description: Verify the heatmap action variant returns the slim shape vs the default richer payload.
tcs.precond: Valid SM JWT; a known tower ID. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call GET /api/v1/towers/:towerId/units (no action).
2. Call GET /api/v1/towers/:towerId/units?action=heatmap.
3. Compare the payload shapes.
tcs.expected: The ?action=heatmap variant returns the slim heatmap shape (id, status, colour); the default returns a richer payload — matching the FSD note that behaviour may vary by ?action=. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm exact field sets per variant.

tcs.scenario: To verify the units endpoint returns the live status/colour for the grid
tcs.description: Verify the units API returns each unit's status and colour bucket used to paint the grid.
tcs.precond: Valid SM JWT; Tower 9 - Triumph tower ID. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access + tower ID.
tcs.steps:
1. Call GET /api/v1/towers/:towerId/units?action=heatmap for Tower 9.
2. Inspect the returned per-unit status and colour fields.
tcs.expected: The response lists units with a status and a colour bucket consistent with the live grid (available/disabled/booked/refuge/pbt/not-available -> green/grey/red). Counts should reconcile with 223 available + 29 disabled + 7 booked + 6 refuge + 2 pbt + 13 not-available = 280. [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact field names.

tcs.scenario: To verify the units endpoint rejects an unauthenticated/expired token
tcs.description: Verify a missing or expired JWT yields 401/403 and no inventory is returned.
tcs.precond: No token / an expired token available. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call GET /api/v1/towers/:towerId/units with no Authorization header.
2. Call the same with an expired JWT.
3. Read the status and body.
tcs.expected: Both calls return 401 (or 403) and no unit inventory is leaked in the body. [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact status code (401 vs 403) and error string not documented in BRD/FRD.

tcs.scenario: To verify a malformed/non-existent towerId is handled gracefully (API)
tcs.description: Verify the units endpoint returns a clean error (not a 500/stack trace) for a bad tower ID.
tcs.precond: Valid SM JWT. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call GET /api/v1/towers/9999999/units (non-existent ID).
2. Call GET /api/v1/towers/not-a-number/units (malformed ID).
3. Read the status and body.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] The backend should return a clean 404 'Tower not found' (or 400 for malformed) with no SQL error and no stack trace leak. Confirm the canonical error response with dev.

tcs.scenario: To verify a 500 / units-API failure shows a graceful error
tcs.description: Verify the page degrades gracefully when the units API errors.
tcs.precond: SM logged in; ability to force/simulate a units-API 500. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] fault injection.
tcs.steps:
1. Select a tower while the units endpoint is forced to return 500 (or blocked).
2. Observe the grid area.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] The grid area should show a friendly error/retry state (not a blank/broken layout or a raw stack trace), and the rest of the page (sidebar, banner) stays intact. Error string not documented in BRD/FRD — confirm with dev.

tcs.scenario: To verify a write (PATCH/POST) from the SM portal is rejected
tcs.description: Verify the SM cannot change tower/unit status via a direct API call.
tcs.precond: Valid SM JWT (roleId=5); a known tower ID. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Using DevTools/Postman with the SM JWT, call PATCH /api/v1/towers/:id with a status-change payload.
2. Inspect the response.
tcs.expected: The API returns 403 Forbidden (or 404 if the route is not exposed to SM); no DB write occurs; the heatmap remains unchanged. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm SM lacks write scope on tower/unit status.

tcs.scenario: To verify viewing the heatmap dispatches no notification
tcs.description: Verify that browsing/clicking the read-only heatmap sends no SMS/WhatsApp/email (silent by design).
tcs.precond: SM logged in. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] outbound message-log visibility.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to the heatmap, switch towers, click available units.
2. Check outbound message logs (SMS/WhatsApp/email) for anything tied to this session.
tcs.expected: No SMS, WhatsApp or email is dispatched from any heatmap interaction — the screen is read-only and silent by design (SM-FS §1.2/§1.7). Silence here is correct, not a bug.

tcs.scenario: To verify an unauthenticated user is redirected to login
tcs.description: Verify that accessing /sales-manager/towers with no session redirects to the SM login.
tcs.precond: No SM JWT in browser storage.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /sales-manager/towers directly.
2. Observe the redirect.
tcs.expected: The user is redirected to the /sales-manager login (mobile OTP entry); the towers/units API is not called and no inventory is leaked.

tcs.scenario: To verify unauthenticated access returns to the default landing after login
tcs.description: Verify that after logging in (from a blocked towers deep-link) the SM lands on the default page.
tcs.precond: No active SM session (auth state cleared).
tcs.steps:
1. Clear cookies and automation-repository/fixtures/.auth/sales-manager.json.
2. Navigate directly to https://uat-web.xrportal.in/sales-manager/towers.
3. Complete OTP login.
tcs.expected: The deep-link redirects to the /sales-manager login screen. Heatmap content is not rendered. After successful OTP login the SM is returned to the Callback Requests landing page (default per SM-FRD §6, DOC_DRIFT-004) — NOT directly back to towers. [VERIFY WITH DEV] whether post-login deep-link return is intended.

tcs.scenario: To verify the SM-role gate — only roles 5 and 4 can access
tcs.description: Verify a non-SM user cannot log into the SM portal and reach the heatmap.
tcs.precond: A user with a role other than 5 (Sales Manager) or 4 (Sales Manager Admin). [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a non-SM mobile.
tcs.steps:
1. Attempt OTP login at /sales-manager with a non-SM mobile.
2. If login succeeds, attempt to access /sales-manager/towers.
tcs.expected: Per SM-FRD §7 and SM-BRD §2, only roles 5 and 4 can log into the SM portal; Admin (role 1) cannot log in via the SM login page (separate auth) though admins can access the same routes via their own portal. Non-SM users are denied at login.

tcs.scenario: To verify a tampered JWT forces a redirect to login on the towers route
tcs.description: Verify that editing the stored JWT causes the protected towers call to fail and redirect.
tcs.precond: SM logged in on /sales-manager/towers.
tcs.steps:
1. Open DevTools -> Application -> storage and change a character in the stored JWT.
2. Reload /sales-manager/towers.
tcs.expected: The towers/units API call fails with 401 and the user is redirected to the /sales-manager login page; no inventory renders. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm tamper-detection at the towers route.

tcs.scenario: To verify direct access to an invalid tower path is handled gracefully
tcs.description: Verify that navigating to a non-existent tower path shows a friendly error, not a crash.
tcs.precond: SM logged in.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate directly to /sales-manager/towers/9999999 (non-existent tower).
2. Observe the page state.
tcs.expected: The page renders the sidebar with valid towers; a friendly 'Tower not found' message replaces the grid area; no JS crash. [VERIFY WITH DEV] whether a per-tower path segment is even routable, or the route ignores it and shows the default tower.

tcs.scenario: To verify the heatmap renders on a tablet viewport
tcs.description: Verify the layout, grid and legend remain usable at 768x1024.
tcs.precond: SM logged in; DevTools viewport set to 768x1024.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /sales-manager/towers at a 768x1024 viewport.
2. Inspect the sidebar, grid and legend.
3. Click a tower to load its grid.
tcs.expected: All elements are visible without page-level horizontal scroll; unit cells are readable; the legend is visible; tower selection works. [VERIFY WITH DEV] the SM portal is mobile-first (SM-BRD §10) — confirm the intended tablet layout.

tcs.scenario: To verify the heatmap on a mobile/phone viewport
tcs.description: Verify the mobile-optimised layout (bottom nav, scrollable grid) at a phone width.
tcs.precond: SM logged in; DevTools viewport set to 375x667.
tcs.steps:
1. Open /sales-manager/towers at 375x667.
2. Inspect the bottom navigation, the tower selector and the grid.
3. Tap a tower, then tap an available unit.
tcs.expected: The page uses the mobile-first layout (bottom navigation bar per SM-BRD §10). The tower selector and grid are reachable (grid may scroll horizontally within its container). Tapping a tower loads its grid; tapping an available unit opens the Unit Details panel. No clipped/overlapping controls. [VERIFY WITH DEV] exact mobile grid behaviour not documented.
